text:
priya: Customer on Node18 + Rollup build reports persistent 401s from our API. They say the SDK keeps retrying and the token manager seems to be duplicated in the bundle. Logs show repeated Authorization attempts then immediate 401, then retry loop.

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro and package config?

priya: Sure — short repro below. Project bundles node_modules into one file with rollup + esbuild plugin. Import style varies (both import and require tested). Steps: 
1) git clone https://example.com/repro.git 
2) npm ci && npm run build 
3) node dist/bundle.js \nObserved: first request returns 401, then SDK retries a few times, every attempt includes the same Authorization header value.

priya: Relevant parts of their package.json and export map: 
```json
{
  "name": "app-repro",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "^1.2.0"
  },
  "rollup": {
    "plugins": ["esbuild"]
  }
}
```
and the SDK export that's being resolved inside the bundle (from node_modules/@redwood/sdk/package.json):
```json
{
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
    },
    "./helpers": "dist/helpers.js"
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

priya: The bundler ends up inlining a deep file (`dist/token-manager.js`) instead of referencing the package entry, which creates a second token manager instance. That second instance doesn't share the runtime credential refresh hooks so Authorization header gets stale and server returns 401.

ryan: This is a classic duplicate-module problem caused by bundlers flattening imports. If the bundler resolves a direct path to a subfile, you can end up with two module copies (one via the package entry, one via deep import). The token manager is a singleton, so duplication breaks state.

julia: Quick workarounds to give the customer: 
- Configure rollup to externalize @redwood/sdk (keep it as node dependency) so the SDK isn't bundled into app code: `external: ["@redwood/sdk"]`.
- Or ensure bundler resolves to package entry by adding an alias/resolve rule that maps `@redwood/sdk/*` -> `node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/*` consistently.
- As a temporary patch, set your bundler to preserve CommonJS interop (rollup-plugin-commonjs) and avoid deep imports.

sam: Short-term patch on our side: release v1.2.4 that adds an explicit `exports` subpath for `./token-manager` and moves token-manager to `dist/runtime/token-manager.js` with a guarded singleton export to tolerate duplicate copies. That should reduce breakage when deep imports happen.

priya: Customer tried the externalize workaround and confirms 401s stopped. They've accepted upgrade path.

alex: Ryan, can you link the PR and a short changelog we can share? Also, let's create a KB entry for "Bundlers that inline SDK duplicates token manager -> 401s / auth retries".

ryan: PR here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 — fixes exports map and adds runtime guard. Changelog blurb: "Fix: prevent duplicated token-manager singletons when SDK is bundled; add stricter exports map to prevent deep imports causing auth retry loops."

julia: I'll draft the KB. Include repro steps, rollup config snippet to externalize, and the note that upgrading to @redwood/sdk@1.2.4 resolves it.

support-bot: Created ticket #5421 and linked PR 432. Notifying eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:

priya: marking this resolved with workaround + scheduled customer upgrade to v1.2.4. Thank you all. :pray:
